name: grove
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A grove is a sacred clearing or wood in Celtic religion, where people held rites of worship. Such spaces of trees formed the holy place called a nemeton. They stood in open land and drew the devotions of the folk.

okr.objective: Present the grove as a sacred space of Celtic worship.
key_results: Groves gave the Celts a scene for rites.
A holy grove could be called a nemeton.
People kept worship in these clearings.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2003
